content: In the Treat All era, it is recommended that all individuals diagnosed with HIV should be promptly started on antiretroviral therapy (ART) to improve treatment outcomes and reduce the risk of new infections. Monitoring the time between diagnosis and treatment initiation, such as within 28 or 90 days, can help assess the quality of care in alignment with national guidelines. The numerator for this indicator is the number of newly diagnosed individuals who begin ART during the reporting period, while the denominator is the total number of individuals newly diagnosed with HIV in the same period. Data for these metrics can be collected from program records, such as HIV testing services (HTS) and ART registers. The recommended reporting period is 12 months, with disaggregation by gender, age, key populations, tuberculosis (TB) status, and time to ART initiation. Index testing and partner notification services aim to identify and test contacts of people living with HIV, including key populations, to increase the diagnosis of HIV-positive individuals. This process should be voluntary and supported by appropriate services. The numerator for this indicator is the number of partners or contacts tested and receiving results, while additional data includes the number of index cases offered and accepting partner services, as well as the number of contacts elicited. Disaggregation includes gender, age, HIV status, and key populations. The distribution of HIV self-test (HIVST) kits is an emerging indicator to monitor trends in self-testing, which is not captured by other HIV testing service indicators. This helps program managers forecast needs for confirmatory testing, ART linkage, and supply chain management. The numerator is the number of HIVST kits distributed, recorded at the lowest distribution point to avoid double counting. Reporting is recommended quarterly, with disaggregation by gender, age, key populations, and HIVST approach. Knowing one’s HIV status is essential for accessing care and reducing transmission. The numerator is the number of respondents who know their HIV-positive status or tested negative in the past year, while the denominator is the total number of respondents. Data is collected through representative surveys, with disaggregation by gender, age, and key populations. The numerator is the number of individuals on ART at the end of the reporting period, excluding those who stopped treatment, died, or were lost to follow-up. The denominator is the estimated number of PLHIV or those who know their HIV status. Retention and attrition analyses are critical for accurate reporting, with disaggregation by gender, age, and key populations. This indicator helps assess retention and identify gaps in care. The numerator includes individuals who stopped ART during the reporting period, while the denominator is the total number of individuals on ART at the start of the period plus new initiations. Disaggregation includes gender, age, key populations, and treatment outcomes. The numerator is the number of individuals with a viral load below 1,000 copies/mL, while the denominator is the total number of individuals on ART for at least six months with a routine viral load test. Disaggregation includes gender, age, and key populations. The numerator is the number of individuals initiating ART with a baseline CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³, while the denominator is the total number of individuals initiating ART with a baseline CD4 count. Disaggregation includes gender, age, and key populations. The numerator is the number of individuals with at least one viral load test result, while the denominator is the total number of individuals on ART for at least six months. Disaggregation includes gender, age, and key populations. The numerator is the number of individuals eligible for viral load testing at six months who received a test and results, while the denominator is the total number eligible for testing. Disaggregation includes gender, age, and key populations. The numerator is the number of individuals receiving a follow-up test, while the denominator is the total number with a viral load ≥1,000 copies/mL. Disaggregation includes gender, age, key populations, and receipt of adherence counseling.
